column1: # Known gaps: our open bugs, each one with a todo behind it, and the sites where the device's own
# READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A ROW. A row here is not an accepted difference and it is not permission
# for anything. It is a gap of ours -- a call plain Metal answers and we refuse, or a field that
# differs with nothing announced to justify it -- which, by the owner's standing rule that what
# Metal allows we must allow, is a bug of ours, written down so the one case that holds it visible
# does not make every run red and teach everyone to stop reading the report. An accepted difference
# lives in `docs/API.md` section 10 and is justified; a degradation lives in the degrade catalogue
# and is announced. This file is neither. Nothing here is resolved by being listed.
# The one kind of row that is not a bug of ours in itself is the device's own answer. The owner's
# rule 1 (AGENTS.md) makes the GPU's native arithmetic and value answers the contract -- maths, NaN
# bits, denormals, rounding, texel, vertex and colour conversions, sampling and filtering,
# resolves -- and the artifact records a note where the device's answer can differ from Metal's.
# The suite declares those notes at the notices site for every case (`replay::NATIVE_NOTES`), and
# they loosen no value: their own definitions say validation derives no tolerance from them. So a
# value the device's native answer moves is a row here, scoped to the venue whose device answers
# so and held both ways like every other row, so a driver that changes its answer forces the edit.
# Its words say what differs, which note records it, whether that note's recorded bound covers
# it, and what is open: nothing, where the bound covers it; the note's documentation, where its
# bound does not state the shape; a measurement, where this run cannot tell the device's answer
# from ours; and our bug, where the difference is not the device's answer at all. No such row asks
# for a form that computes Metal's bits where the device has a native one: rule 1 rules it out.
# It is an EXPECTATION, NOT AN ALLOWLIST, and `conformance replay` holds it to that in both
#   - a refusal or a divergence that is not listed here fails the run: a new gap appeared;
#   - a row listed here that the run no longer holds ALSO fails the run, saying the gap looks
#     fixed and the row must go.
# That second direction is the whole point. Closing a gap forces the ledger edit, so a row cannot
# outlive the bug it stands for and this file cannot rot into a silencer. It also means a row is
# checked by execution rather than by discipline, which is the standard the rest of the suite is
# held to. It has already earned its keep twice in this round: a product fix landed and the replay
# named four stale rows before anyone reasoned about the fix.
# The ledger changes the exit status and nothing else. The report still prints each of these as a
# `Refused` or `Divergent` row, with our answer and Metal's, with Metal's own words where its API
# validation refuses the call too, and counted in the suite's own numbers. Nothing is laundered.
# A row is held only against the cases a run selected and the venues it ran on, so replaying one
# case does not read every other row as fixed, and a run on one venue does not read another
# Tab-separated, SIX fields. Blank lines and lines from `#` are ignored.
#   venue       `*` for every venue, or words held (without case, as a substring) against the
#               venue's own description: its device name, driver and API version.
#               `*` is the STRONGER claim, not the looser one -- the second direction then holds
#               the row on every venue the run selected the case on -- so widening a row's scope
#               makes it harder to satisfy, which is what stops a venue-scoped row from becoming a
#               way to silence a venue. A pattern that matches nothing holds the row nowhere, so
#               its gap reads as unlisted and the run fails: a typo is loud.
#   expects     `refused`, a call plain Metal answered and we did not; or `divergent`, a field that
#               differs with nothing announced to justify it. Nothing else is ever written down:
#               an unrecorded case and a stale recording must fail loudly, and a venue that
#               honestly lacks a feature is not a gap of ours at all.
#   site        the site, as node names from the root, exactly as the report prints it.
#   answer      what the run answers there, exactly as the report prints it after the site, which
#               `conformance replay` also emits as a ready-to-paste row so nobody has to
#               reconstruct it. For a refusal that is our typed error. For a divergence it is how
#               much moved: how many of the site's leaves differ and the largest difference where
#               the values are numbers. NOT the first mismatch -- a bound read off the first
#               mismatch is not a bound (four rotated-target rows differ by one code at their
#               first mismatch and reach two well past it), and a walk position is a property of
#               the data rather than of the bug, so it would rename the row whenever an earlier
#               leaf moved. The report prints that position on the line below, where it helps a
#               reader and binds nothing. Part of the row's identity, so a gap that changed into
#               another gap at the same site is a new gap and not this one.
#   waiting on  the open bug, in words: what Metal does, what we do instead, and where the fix
#               belongs. Not matched -- it is what a reader needs -- but a row must carry one.
# A row whose case is not in the tree yet cannot be committed: a test holds every live row to a
# case that exists AND to a site that case's committed recording actually holds, so a row for a
# site the case never produces is impossible rather than silently unheld. Leave such a row here as
# a `#` comment for the stream that owns the case; nothing is waiting today.

column5: Err(Error::Bind("the bind state was refused: Unsupported(Unsupported { feature: MeshShading, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: None })"))
column6: The runtime refuses `drawMeshThreads` where the threads leave a partial object threadgroup, `Unsupported(MeshShading, NotImplemented)` out of the bind state (crates/metal2vulkan/src/bind/graphics.rs, `mesh_draw`'s `threads[i].is_multiple_of(lo[i])` test), while Metal draws it and runs the threads left over. Not a device gap: this M3 Max has mesh shading and draws every other row of the same probe. Measured on it (macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, our probe gaps/mesh/obj, one shape per process): the draw launches ceil(threads/L) object threadgroups, `threads_per_grid` is the threads asked for, and the last threadgroup on an axis runs with the threads left over as a non-uniform threadgroup exactly as `dispatchThreads:` does for compute - `threads_per_threadgroup` is min(L, threads - group*L) per axis (6 of 64 reports 6), `thread_position_in_threadgroup` and `thread_index_in_threadgroup` run over that reduced size, `simdgroups_per_threadgroup` is ceil of it over 32, and a threadgroup barrier synchronizes the threads left over alone. The cause is that Vulkan has no partial workgroup: the exact form is the one compute already uses, a region per edge dispatched at its own local size, which for a draw means several draws of several pipeline specializations and, on a grid with more than one whole threadgroup on a higher axis, a primitive order that is not Metal's; the alternative is one draw of ceil groups with the object entry reading its reduced size from its `DispatchRegion` record (`MultiRegion` 1 already carries the grid and L, and already reports ceil threadgroups and the asked-for threads), deriving the thread position and index from `lin` over that size and returning before the body past it, which is exact for everything but a threadgroup barrier and so needs a pipeline variant whose compile refuses an object function that synchronizes. Neither is built. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

Metal counts the quads the discard drops whole in a simdgroup sum that sits ahead of the discard for a measured reason -- the discard's condition reads the sum (`counted_dependent`), or a device store (`counted_store`) or an atomic (`counted_atomic`) lies between them -- so each kept texel's first channel, `before > after`, is 1. On the gate container's arm64 lavapipe (`llvmpipe (LLVM 21.1.8, 128 bits)`, the venue this row names) all four texels of the kept quad read 0, uniformly and each by exactly one code: our run's sum saw the same lane count before and after the discard. MoltenVK on this M3 Max answers Metal's 1 exactly, with no notice, so this is one venue's difference and not the module's rule being wrong (verified: a whole-set replay on each venue, 2026-10-23). The suite's other lavapipe, `llvmpipe (LLVM 23.1.1, 256 bits)` on x86-64, does not hold it and carries no row for this case, which is why the venue field names the 128-bit build rather than the bare substring `llvmpipe` that covers both: a row scoped to both read as stale on a venue the gap was never measured on. Two llvmpipe builds that differ in vector width and in LLVM release answering differently makes this the build's and not the module's, and it still does not say which of the two candidates below it is. The cause is NOT established, and the case as written cannot establish it: the four numbers it records per texel are identical under both candidates -- the device's fragment simdgroup holding only the kept quad, so the dropped quads were never in it (the target is 8 by 4, exactly one 32-lane simdgroup if the device packs it that way), and the device's compiler moving the reduction past the discard although `canon/discard_sink.rs` placed it ahead on purpose. Both give before == after and so (0, 0, 0, 0), on every texel alike, which is why the uniformity across the quad separates nothing either. The next step is the case's: record the simdgroup's own size and the raw `before` and `after` beside the four derived numbers, which separates the two at no cost, then fix whichever it is -- a device whose reduction does not see the dropped lanes needs the active set computed in the module rather than taken from the device's implicit one (crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/simd/group.rs with crates/metal2vulkan-air/src/canon/discard_sink.rs), and a device whose fragment simdgroup is smaller than Metal's is a different answer again. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list, handed to whoever takes the discard-hoist family.

column5: Err(Error::Unsupported("unsupported: Unsupported { feature: Format, needs: NotImplemented, location: Some(RenderPipeline at Color(0)), symbol: None }"))
column6: Plain Metal on this M3 Max makes and runs a render pipeline whose ARGB8Unorm colour attachment blends with DestinationAlpha and OneMinusDestinationAlpha in the COLOUR factors, and stores every texel as the RGBA8Unorm leg's bytes rotated (recorded here over 3 runs, 8,192 texels, zero mismatches; Metal's own API validation let it run). The runtime refuses the pipeline Unsupported(Format, NotImplemented) at colour attachment 0, so the refusal is of something plain Metal does. The cause is structural rather than a policy: the runtime holds ARGB8Unorm in an R8G8B8A8_UNORM image of the rotated bytes, so the image's alpha channel carries Metal's BLUE and a colour factor that must read Metal's destination alpha would have to read the image's red. Vulkan has no such blend factor. The alpha-factor direction is already solved -- a second pipeline output of copies of Metal's source alpha (pipeline::rotated_blend) -- but that trick does not reach a DESTINATION channel, which only the framebuffer holds. The exact forms are a pass that keeps the rotated image's channels in Metal's order behind a swizzled view, or reading the destination in the fragment where the device offers programmable blending. Neither is built. Fix belongs in metal2vulkan's pipeline (rotated_blend) and the runtime's ARGB8Unorm image layout. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

Metal's `MTLComputePipelineDescriptor.reset` is PARTIAL. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434), from `compute-descriptor-reset`'s own committed recording over three runs: the reset restores the label to nil, every `buffers[i].mutability` to `MTLMutabilityDefault`, `supportIndirectCommandBuffers` and `supportAddingBinaryFunctions` to false and `maxCallStackDepth` to 1, and leaves its three thread-shape properties exactly as the program set them -- `threadGroupSizeIsMultipleOfThreadExecutionWidth` true, `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` 96, `requiredThreadsPerThreadgroup` 8 by 6 by 2. The runtime has no descriptor object, so the coverage map's counterpart for `reset` is `ComputePipelineDescriptor::new` (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/descriptor.rs), a fresh value that resets all nine, and our side answers 0, 0 and false where Metal answers what was set. Nothing is announced for it, so by the standing rule it is a gap of ours. It is also very likely an Apple defect rather than a contract: in the same round `MTLTileRenderPipelineDescriptor.reset` restores the analogous `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup`, `requiredThreadsPerThreadgroup` and `threadgroupSizeMatchesTileSize` correctly (`tile-descriptor-reset` is exact) and `MTLMeshRenderPipelineDescriptor.reset` restores every field it has (`mesh-descriptor-reset` is exact), so only the compute descriptor keeps anything. The fix is a choice between two forms and neither may be guessed at: a `ComputePipelineDescriptor::reset` that mirrors Metal's three kept fields, or an accepted difference in docs/API.md section 10 saying a reset compute descriptor keeps its thread shape on Metal and not here. Mirroring an Apple bug in a published crate's API is the owner's call, so this is on the orchestrator's todo list rather than fixed here. Not a device gap: no venue is involved -- the difference is Metal's recorded answer against a plain Rust struct, so the row is every venue's.

`BinaryArchive` has three of Metal's four pipeline adders: `addMeshRenderPipelineFunctionsWithDescriptor:error:` has no counterpart at all. Metal takes the call, takes it a second time with the same descriptor, and then serialises the archive to a file that exists and holds bytes (measured on this M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1, from this case's own committed recording over three runs, plain Metal and under its API validation, which let the case run). Ours cannot be asked: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/binary_archive/mod.rs declares `add_compute_pipeline_functions` (:138), `add_render_pipeline_functions` (:161) and `add_tile_render_pipeline_functions` (:194) and no mesh form, and the module's own documentation lists the three as if they were all of them. The pieces for the fourth are already there: `metal2vulkan::pipeline::MeshPipelineDescriptor` exists and the runtime creates mesh states from it (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/pipeline/render.rs:629), and the add's own shape is the render one -- create the state with `Some(&used)`, then keep what it used under the descriptor's archive keys -- so what is missing is the key function beside `metal_key::render` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/binary_archive/metal_key.rs:185) for an object-plus-mesh-plus-fragment triple, and the `check` arm that refuses a mesh creation on a miss (`binary_archive::check` is already called for the mesh path at crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/pipeline/render.rs:1579, where the comment says outright that no archive holds a mesh render pipeline). It is deliberately NOT done here: adding `BinaryArchive::add_mesh_render_pipeline_functions` adds an item to a published crate's public surface and a new archive key form to its container, which needs docs/REFUSALS.md regenerated and the `api_surface` table updated, and this stream took no evidence for either. Every venue's: the gap is in the runtime's own API, before any Vulkan call. Open: for whoever takes the runtime's archive surface.

Metal accepts a **metallib** as a binary archive and we refuse it. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this case's own committed recording over three runs: `newBinaryArchiveWithDescriptor:error:` with the descriptor's `url` set to a metallib of the case's own shader answers an archive, where the same call over a text file, an empty file, a missing path and a directory each answers `MTLBinaryArchiveDomain` code 1 (the four rows this case compares beside it, all four of which we match exactly). What Metal does with such an archive is not measured here -- whether it holds anything, or is simply an empty archive that happens to have read a container it recognises -- and that is the first thing the fix needs. Ours refuses at `container::read` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/binary_archive/container.rs:183), which reads the file whole and hands it to `decode`, whose first act is to check the suite-private magic `M2VBARCH` and a version word (container.rs:116, the magic at :37); a metallib starts `MTLB`, so `decode` answers `None` and the creation becomes `BinaryArchive(InvalidFile)` (container.rs:240). By the owner's standing rule that what Metal allows we must allow, the refusal is the bug. The fix is to decide what a non-archive container means and say so: either accept a file that parses as a metallib as an archive that holds no entry (which is what Metal's answer is consistent with, and which `Library::from_metallib` can already tell), or keep refusing and record an accepted difference in docs/API.md section 10. Metal's `MTLAttributeStrideStatic` on a `[[stage_in]]` layout of `MTLBufferLayoutStrideDynamic` is not "read at stride 0"; it fetches the element at the bind offset for the FIRST element and hands every element past it ZERO. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from these cases' own committed recordings: a dynamic layout over a buffer holding `0x10 + e` at element `e`, eight threads stepping by thread position in x at rate 1, bound with the constant, answered `0x110` and then `0x100` seven times (the fixture writes the attribute plus `0x100`), while a bind at stride 0 answered `0x110` eight times -- so the two are different answers and Metal's validation stops neither. The same shape at a bind offset of 8 answered `0x112` and then `0x100` seven times, which says the bind offset still reaches the first element. Ours answers the stride-0 reading: `attribute_stride` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/argument_table.rs:377) maps the constant to `None`, `None` removes the index's entry from `ArgumentTable::attribute_strides`, and every reader of that map takes a missing entry as 0 -- the binder's push constant `PushField::StageInStride` (crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/stage_io/stage_in.rs:179, whose own module note at line 28 says "as 0 for a buffer bound without one") and the reach check (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/fetch_reach.rs:112). So the fetch walks elements at stride 0 and every thread reads element 0, which is a silently wrong answer rather than a refusal. The runtime already knows the real behaviour for ONE of the four setters: `ComputeCommandEncoder::set_bytes_with_stride` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/compute.rs:607) documents "an M4 read element 0 of the bytes and zeros past it" and refuses that combination `NotImplemented(KernelStageIn)` rather than emulating it -- this oracle shows the buffer forms behave the same way, so the note on the buffer forms (argument_table.rs:377 and compute.rs:509, "one bound without a stride reads at stride 0") is what is wrong, not the inline-bytes one. The fix belongs in the fetch, not in the table: `PushField::StageInStride` needs to be able to say "the constant was bound" apart from "stride 0" -- a sentinel value or a flag beside it -- and the pulled read in crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/stage_io/stage_in.rs must then select the element at the bind offset where the element index is 0 and a zero of the attribute's form otherwise, which is the same predicate the inline-bytes form would need and would let that refusal be dropped too. It is deliberately NOT done here: this stream's target is the conformance suite, the change is to a published crate's shader lowering and its push-constant ABI (so it moves `SEMANTICS_VERSION` and every stage-in recording), and it needs release-mode evidence this stream has not taken. Scoped to every venue because the gap is in the push constant and the fetch's own arithmetic, before any device behaviour -- measured on this M3 Max alone, so every other venue is expected and unaudited. Open: for whoever takes the runtime's stage-in fetch.

Metal's `texture2d<half>` never widens, so a 16-bit float texel's NaN comes back as its own code -- sign, payload and signalling bit kept -- and ours answers the one positive quiet NaN `0x7e00` for every one of them. This M3's decode of such a texel into `f32` canonicalizes the NaN, so the code is gone before any conversion of ours sees it; no finite, zero, denormal or infinite texel differs anywhere, and the count is the same at every site. The translation reads every site through the device's decode, the GPU's native answer. Announced `device-nan-encoding`, whose definition in `pipeline/artifact.rs` says validation derives no tolerance from it, so the rows stay divergent.

column5: Err(Error::Unsupported("unsupported: Unsupported { feature: Format, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: Some(\"MTLPixelFormatASTC_4x2_sRGB\") }"))
column6: The runtime answers Metal's heap footprint for ASTC's 4x2 and 8x4 footprints, which is arithmetic over a descriptor, but holds no image of any of them, so `newTextureWithDescriptor:` is refused `Unsupported(Format, NotImplemented)` out of the translator's format table (crates/metal2vulkan/src/metal/format/mod.rs, the `formats_named_not_held!` and `astc_without_a_vulkan_block!` patterns, whose `repr` is `NotImplemented`; the refusal reaches this site through `image_error` in crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/texture.rs). Measured on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, in a throwaway process forked per (format, texture type): Metal answers a size and an alignment for every descriptor of this case, makes a texture of every format in every texture type bar the ones the case's own module records, and takes a host round trip through each. The whole of Metal's answer is in this case's recording, which is what an implementation will be held to. The case STOPS at this first refusal by design: the runtime holds no image of any of the 33 formats of the family, so recording a refusal per site and going on would print some 2900 `Refused` rows and need a ledger row for each. So this one row stands for the family, and the open work -- an image for each format -- is on the orchestrator's todo list with the measurements. Scoped `*` and not to a venue: the refusal is decided by the format table before any device is consulted, so no device can change it; verified on MoltenVK over this M3 Max (2026-10-25), unverified elsewhere by execution.

column5: Err(Error::Unsupported("unsupported: Unsupported { feature: Format, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: Some(\"MTLPixelFormatARGB8Unorm_sRGB\") }"))
column6: Plain Metal makes a texture of `ARGB8Unorm_sRGB` in all eight non-multisample texture types and takes a host `replaceRegion:`/`getBytes:` round trip through each (an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, in a throwaway process forked per (format, texture type); the whole of its answer is in this case's recording). The runtime refuses `newTextureWithDescriptor:` `Unsupported(Format, NotImplemented)` out of the translator's format table (crates/metal2vulkan/src/metal/format/mod.rs, the `formats_named_not_held!` pattern, whose `repr` is `NotImplemented`; the refusal reaches this site through `image_error` in crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/texture.rs). The cause is NOT that the bytes have no Vulkan format: they are `ARGB8Unorm`'s (alpha in byte 0, then red, green and blue), which this crate holds in `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` read through a rotating view, and `fill_value.rs` already states this format's own layout as a linear alpha byte and three sRGB bytes. It is that no Vulkan format applies the sRGB transfer function to the three channels Metal's does: every Vulkan `_SRGB` format encodes the word's low three components and leaves the fourth linear, so the function would land on Metal's alpha and miss Metal's blue. A view's component mapping cannot move it, because format conversion runs before the component swizzle, so `R8G8B8A8_SRGB` under `ARGB8Unorm`'s rotation would read Metal's alpha sRGB-decoded and Metal's blue linear -- two channels of four wrong, which is not a near-equivalent a precision note could carry. The exact form is the one a device that cannot sample an 8-bit sRGB format already takes: hold the codes in a UNORM image (here `ARGB8Unorm`'s `R8G8B8A8_UNORM` image through its rotating view) and decode them in the shader through Metal's twelve-bit table (`metal::format::srgb_raw_twin`, `metal::texel_format::srgb_twin_on`, `RuntimeFact::SrgbTexture`, `lower::arith::srgb`), here as the only read of the format on every device, since no view of this image decodes it, so a clear, a blit and a colour attachment of it must take the same route. That is not built. Open: translator and runtime work, in metal2vulkan's format table and the UNORM twin's format map with the runtime's image plan and binder. Its sibling straggler `BGRA4Unorm` is held, which is why the case reaches this format. Scoped `*` and not to a venue: the refusal is decided by the format table before any device is consulted, so no device can change it; verified on MoltenVK over this M3 Max (2026-10-25), unverified elsewhere by execution.

Ours reads the image as `f32` lanes and rounds them (`lower::texture::metal_texel_nans` keeps the device's decode for a half-channel class, which is exact only on a device that widens a half texel exactly), and this device's **sampler** canonicalizes a 16-bit float texel's NaN to 0xFFC00000, its own negative quiet NaN, so every NaN lane of a nearest sample reads 0xFE00 where Metal reads the texel's code. Metal rasterizes a line by the diamond-exit rule and this driver's Bresenham mode breaks one tie the other way. The line of vertices 0 and 1 runs exactly through the boundary point (3.5, 1.0), a vertex of the diamonds of both pixels either side of it: Metal draws the lower pixel (row 1 column 3) and leaves row 0 column 3 at the pass's clear, and this driver draws row 0 column 3 and leaves row 1 column 3. Those two texels, and nothing else, are the whole of each cell's difference -- the mark word alone, since the fragment's vertex id is 0 either way. Vulkan's Bresenham diamond is the open set |p - x| + |q - y| < 0.5, so a line that only touches a vertex exits no diamond and the specification requires no fragment for either pixel; both choices conform, and llvmpipe (LLVM 23.1.1, Mesa 26.2.4) makes Metal's. The runtime already asks every line-rasterizing pipeline for VK_LINE_RASTERIZATION_MODE_BRESENHAM_EXT (`pipeline/graphics.rs`), which is what took these four cells from 7, 7, 5 and 13 texels to these two: without it a strictLines device covers the whole rectangle of the line's width. There is no Vulkan control over the tie, so this is the driver's own and not the runtime's. RADV and ANV unrun. docs/FAST-PATHS.md carries the gap.

This is NOT a rounding difference and it is not the narrow-float NaN rows of the same case. Metal's `float4` fetch of an `MTLVertexFormatFloatRGB9E5` attribute answers 1.0 (0x3F800000) in the fourth component, the missing-component default of a three-channel format, and we answer 0 (0x0) -- the first differing element of every one of these sites. Beyond the default, the `float4` and `half4` legs move 32 of the site's elements with a bound of 65407, close to the format's largest representable value (65408), so this device's decode of the shared 5-bit exponent parts from Metal's as well, where the `instance-step` leg's 12 differing elements all move by exactly 1 and are consistent with the fourth-component default alone. The cause is that the format is handed to Vulkan's fixed-function vertex input as `VK_FORMAT_E5B9G9R9_UFLOAT_PACK32` (crates/metal2vulkan/src/metal/vertex.rs), and that packed shared-exponent format is not one a driver must offer as a vertex buffer format at all. The translator's own pulled decode is right about both halves: `components` in crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/stage_io/fetch.rs computes `m * 2^(e - 24)`, which is exact for a 9-bit mantissa, and `decode` fills a missing fourth component with 1.0. This is capability and Metal's contract, not the device's arithmetic: the missing component's default is no value the device computes, and a vertex format the device need not offer is implemented. So the fix is to stop handing this format to fixed-function input -- pull the fetch, or carry the Metal format in `VertexFetch::FixedFunction` so the plan can fill the missing component after the load. Which path each leg of this case takes on this device is NOT established by this run; the two legs' different bounds say they differ. Open: translator work, on the orchestrator's todo list.

Metal's compute pipeline state answers `staticThreadgroupMemoryLength` 24576 -- the fixture's own 24 KiB `threadgroup` array -- and we answer 32768 on this venue. Metal DROPS what a shader or the blit engine writes into memory whose backing is read-only, silently and with no error, and we land the write. Metal's rule is measured, not assumed: `probes/readonly_gpu_writes.m` ran eleven shapes on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, one shape a process, eight runs a shape, each against a writable twin of the same program, and a kernel's stores and a pass's visibility result both complete with no error while neither a later command buffer nor the CPU sees any of it -- the writable twin landing its write in all three places is what makes 'dropped' a measurement. The two read-only states agree: bit 24 of `MTLResourceOptions` (what this case states, `ResourceOptions::PRIVATE_BIT`) and the production SPI pair `detachBacking` plus `replaceBackingWithRanges:readOnly:YES` answer alike on all ten shapes measurable under both. The owner's standing rule is that where Metal drops such a write we drop it too, on EVERY driver, with no refusal. We do it on macOS alone: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/read_only_view.rs imports the pages through a read-only view of them (`mach_vm_remap` then `mprotect`), and `VIEWS_DROP_WRITES` is `cfg!(target_os = "macos")`, so on a Linux driver the import is of the caller's own pages, the GPU's writes reach them, and the difference is announced as `Degradation::PrivateResourceOption`. The announcement is not a justification here: the case declares nothing of it and the bytes differ. What the exact form is on a Linux driver is NOT established -- the module's own measurement is that those drivers pin imported pages for writing and refuse or fault on read-only ones (`host_memory.rs`), so the read-only-view trick does not carry over -- and finding one is the work this row waits on. The read taken in the SAME command buffer is exact here, which is the module's recorded reading that a dropped write may be read back from the GPU's caches and is not a contract; the two sites that move are the later command buffer's read and the CPU's. Open: runtime work, on the orchestrator's todo list.

Metal's `MTLStoreActionDontCare` leaves the attachment holding the texels it held BEFORE the pass, and we leave what the pass rendered. Metal's answer is this case's own committed recording on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1 and it is sharper than a guess would be: under `DontCare` then `MTLLoadActionLoad` pass A's clear AND its draw are both gone and the host's per-texel write survives in pass A's own region. The four cells of this case that diverge here are exactly the `MTLStoreActionDontCare` ones, and the eight that do not are untouched, so the sequence, the render-area bounds and both load actions are right -- it is the store alone. The cause is deliberate and documented: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/render_target.rs hands Vulkan `DONT_CARE` only on a driver measured to keep one of Metal's two answers (`DriverFact::DontCareStoreIsMetals` or `DontCareStoreIsOneOfMetals`, MoltenVK on the M4 and the M3 Max) and stores the attachment (`STORE`) on every other, because Vulkan leaves a `DONT_CARE` attachment's contents undefined and a driver may answer a third thing neither of Metal's -- the module records NVIDIA's leaving a pass's clear under its draw. `STORE` is Metal's OTHER answer, the one its tiler gives on overflow, so it is a recorded near-equivalent and the runtime announces `dont-care-store` for it; but it is not the answer this case's Metal recording holds, and a program that reads such an attachment after the pass sees pass A's result here where Metal gives it the prior texels. The exact form is to restore those texels rather than pick one of Metal's answers: keep them and put them back around the pass, the shape `kept_bytes.rs` already uses for a texture over a buffer, which costs a copy per `DontCare` attachment -- so by the owner's fast-default rule it belongs behind a `DevicePolicy` switch with its docs/FAST-PATHS.md row and `STORE` stays the default. column6: Metal resolves a multisampled depth/stencil attachment with the stencil filter `MTLMultisampleStencilResolveFilterSample0` under the depth filter `Min` or `Max`, and we refuse it `NotImplemented(DepthStencilResolve)`. Ours is not a device refusal dressed up: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/resolve.rs states in its own words that a filter the device's resolve modes lack -- `supportedDepthResolveModes`, `supportedStencilResolveModes`, or the other aspect's modes where a subpass resolving one aspect must name the same mode for both, read off the compile device's description as `VkProperty::{DepthResolveMode, StencilResolveMode, IndependentResolveNone, IndependentResolve}` -- is 'not built', and names the exact path in the same sentence: a resolve DRAW, which the module already uses for other unresolvable pairs and which needs no resolve mode from the device at all. So the gap is work not done rather than a capability missing, which is what makes it ours under the owner's rule that what Metal allows we must allow. This venue is a device with no independent resolve of the two aspects, so the `Sample0` stencil filter cannot be named beside a `Min` or `Max` depth one; the case's other filter pairs run here, so it is these two cells. The fix belongs in resolve.rs: reach the resolve draw for a filter pair the device's modes cannot state, as the module does where `DepthResolvedSample` follows `Min` or `Max` on a sampled attachment. column6: Metal resolves a multisampled depth/stencil attachment with the stencil filter `MTLMultisampleStencilResolveFilterSample0` under the depth filter `Min` or `Max`, and we refuse it `NotImplemented(DepthStencilResolve)`. Ours is not a device refusal dressed up: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/resolve.rs states in its own words that a filter the device's resolve modes lack -- `supportedDepthResolveModes`, `supportedStencilResolveModes`, or the other aspect's modes where a subpass resolving one aspect must name the same mode for both, read off the compile device's description as `VkProperty::{DepthResolveMode, StencilResolveMode, IndependentResolveNone, IndependentResolve}` -- is 'not built', and names the exact path in the same sentence: a resolve DRAW, which the module already uses for other unresolvable pairs and which needs no resolve mode from the device at all. So the gap is work not done rather than a capability missing, which is what makes it ours under the owner's rule that what Metal allows we must allow. This venue is a device with no independent resolve of the two aspects, so the `Sample0` stencil filter cannot be named beside a `Min` or `Max` depth one; the case's other filter pairs run here, so it is these two cells. The fix belongs in resolve.rs: reach the resolve draw for a filter pair the device's modes cannot state, as the module does where `DepthResolvedSample` follows `Min` or `Max` on a sampled attachment. So the number is honest about the device and a dispatch past it is refused typed -- which this family's own test `a_dispatch_the_device_cannot_take_is_the_devices_gap` rules is the DEVICE's gap and verdicts `LacksFeature`. The open work is that the same ruling has not reached the FACT: the state's reported limit is compared against Metal's number as if it were an answer of ours, so a venue whose threadgroup is smaller reads as a divergence at the getter while the matching dispatch reads as the venue's honest gap. Plain Metal TAKES a sparse mapping update whose slice is past the texture's own slices, and it reaches real memory; the runtime maps nothing and counts nothing for it (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/sparse/mapping.rs, `UnitGrid::clipped_size`, which answers None for a slice past the texture's). Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434) from this case's own committed recording, 3 runs and one outcome, over a two-slice 256x256 nine-level R32Float sparse texture whose level 0 holds 4 by 4 of Metal's 16-KiB tiles with two tiles of each slice mapped and filled with four distinct bytes: a Map of one tile of slice 2 raises the heap's usedSize by exactly one page (65,536 to 81,920), an Unmap of another tile of slice 2 does NOT give that page back (81,920 after it and after the reads), and the texels say the page reached a real tile -- a 16 by 16 texel block at texel (0, 16) of slice 0's tile (0, 0), 256 of its 4,096 words, reads 0xFFFFFFFF, which probes/sparse_unmapped_blit.m measured on this chip to be Metal's unwritten pattern, where every other word of that tile and all 4,096 words of the other three tiles still hold their own fill. So Metal binds a page at an address its own out-of-bounds slice produced and part of it lands inside an in-bounds mapped tile, which its own API validation layer refuses the call to prevent. Ours maps nothing, counts nothing and loses no texel, which is why all four sites differ. The exact form is NOT derivable from what is measured: the address the page landed at is Apple's internal page layout for this chip and nothing here says what rule produced it, and which of the two out-of-bounds steps did it is unmeasured because the case reads once after both. The next step is a probe that separates the Map from the Unmap and reads every tile of both slices, which would say whether one page lands in several tiles at once; mirroring an Apple page-binding accident in a published crate is the owner's call either way. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

Plain Metal reads back only a FRACTION of a sparse tile a move rebound, and we read the whole of it. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434) from these cases' own committed recordings, 3 runs and one outcome each, over a 256x256 nine-level R32Float sparse texture whose level 0 holds 4 by 4 of Metal's 16-KiB tiles: a destination tile the move landed a source tile on reads ZERO except for 128 of its 4,096 words, which hold the source tile's own marker and sit in 4-by-2 texel groups at a 16-by-16 stride -- sixteen groups of 32 bytes, 512 bytes of the 16-KiB page. Ours reads the source tile's marker in all 4,096 words, which is why 3,968 of them differ at each site. WHAT IS NOT THE GAP: the move's own rule. The destination run, the source clipping and the no-wrap behaviour all match exactly -- sparse-mapping-move-of-a-source-past-the-level compares every texel of six tiles and is compliant, and in these cases the source's marker appears at exactly the destination tile Metal's run names and at no other, so what differs is how much of the moved tile a later blit can read and not where the tile went. It is NOT an out-of-bounds artefact: sparse-mapping-move-inside-the-level has both sides wholly inside the level and its validated leg reads `ran`, and all four of its destination tiles read this way. It is not a property of the tile's position either: B(1,1) reads whole in sparse-mapping-move-of-a-clipped-source and partial in sparse-mapping-move-inside-the-level. Which tiles read partially is fixed for a given program, which points at Apple's own page layout for that program -- the same class of thing as sparse-mapping-a-slice-past-the-textures. The 4-by-2-at-16-by-16 shape is the shape of a lossless-compression block's head, so the likely mechanism is that Metal's moved page carries compressed payload whose metadata the destination texture does not have, and a blit resolves only each block's uncompressed head; the runtime's emulated sparse path moves real memory, so the whole tile reads back (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/sparse/, where a fix would belong). The exact form is NOT derivable from what is measured: nothing here says what rule picks the 128 words, and reproducing an Apple compression-metadata mismatch in a published crate is the owner's call. The next step is a probe that reads a moved tile under several formats and page sizes and says whether the surviving words are a compression block's head. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.
